business: StoreLab (A/B testing for physical retail: simulate store layout and display changes on your own store's data before moving a shelf)
by_segment: Commercial or category director at a 200-500 store chain
Head of operations or merchandising at a 60-200 store chain
Owner-operator of a 20-60 store regional chain
why_not: Even at the 10-store minimum that's PHP 80,000 a month, almost a million a year, locked in for 12 months with a company that has zero results to show me. For that money I could hire several merchandisers and just run a real pilot in a few stores myself.
I can't take a 12-month, roughly PHP 960,000 commitment to the board for a company with zero customer results. A simulation is only as good as its track record, and nobody has shown me theirs.

Ten stores minimum at PHP 8,000 each is PHP 80,000 a month, almost a million pesos locked in for a year, right after a slow quarter when I'm being told to cut. That money hires several more store staff, and I can see what staff do for me.

Ten stores minimum at 8,000 each is 80,000 pesos a month, almost a million a year locked in, and that buys several more staff for my stores. A new company with no results can't show me how I get that back within the year.

Most of my endcaps and displays are proposed and paid for by the brands, I mostly just approve placement, so I don't see why I'd pay close to a million pesos a year to simulate something suppliers already fund. After a slow quarter I'm cutting costs, not signing 12-month contracts with a company that has zero customer results.

Most of our endcaps and displays are proposed and paid for by the brands, and I just approve placement and fix things myself on weekend visits. Locking in almost a million pesos a year, at the 10-store minimum for 12 months, to simulate layouts we mostly don't design ourselves is hard to justify, especially from a company with no results yet.
